stories.headline: Italy leads EU push for sanctions against Israeli minister Ben-Gvir over Flotilla activists abuse
stories.summary: Israel intercepted the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters on May 20, detaining 430 activists including 29 Italians. Video posted by Israeli Security Minister Ben-Gvir showing activists blindfolded and kneeling provoked unified condemnation from Mattarella, Meloni, Tajani, and Crosetto; Italy formally requested EU sanctions against Ben-Gvir through Kallas, who accepted the request for discussion at the June 15 Foreign Affairs Council. France banned Ben-Gvir from its territory; Salvini's initially muted response ('he shouldn't have done it') diverged from coalition partners.

stories.headline: Local elections across 750 Italian municipalities test party standings ahead of 2027 national vote
stories.summary: Italian voters went to the polls on May 24–25 in approximately 750 municipalities including key cities Venice, Reggio Calabria, Salerno, and Avellino; the elections are widely read as a bellwether for the 2027 national elections, with centrodestra defending Venice and centrosinistra pushing for gains, De Luca running in Salerno without the official PD symbol fracturing the coalition there, and Vannacci's Futuro Nazionale making its first significant local electoral test.

stories.headline: Italy's bid for EU Stability Pact flexibility on energy spending rebuffed by Lagarde; government extends fuel excise cuts, averts truckers' strike
stories.summary: Meloni's formal request to the European Commission to extend the national escape clause — used for defense spending — to cover energy costs was publicly rejected by ECB President Lagarde on Italian television on May 24, who told Rome to respect fiscal rules; the government also passed a Council of Ministers decree extending fuel excise tax cuts through early June and providing €200M to truckers, defusing a threatened transport strike. Internal coalition tension between Crosetto (pushing for EU SAFE instrument funds for defense) and Economy Minister Giorgetti (urging caution on debt) featured prominently, and Reuters reported Italy faces a €50 billion investment gap to meet EU renewable energy targets.

stories.headline: 34th anniversary of the Capaci massacre commemorated by Mattarella, Meloni, and party leaders
stories.summary: Italy marked the 34th anniversary of the May 23, 1992 Capaci bombing that killed judge Giovanni Falcone, his wife Francesca Morvillo, and three escort agents; President Mattarella issued a major statement declaring 'the mafia will end' and calling the attack 'the beginning of civil resistance,' while Meloni and M5S leader Conte attended separate commemorations in Palermo and Sicily.

stories.headline: Two Parma teachers attacked by student gang; Defense Minister Crosetto demands harsh consequences
stories.summary: A group of students assaulted two teachers near the Parco della Musica in Parma on May 22, with video of the attack spreading on social media; Defense Minister Crosetto called for zero tolerance and 'severe consequences for all involved,' triggering a public row with local school authorities who argued schools should educate rather than punish. The incident sparked nationwide political debate on youth violence and school safety.
